title: Streaming proxy adapter and behavior-flag orchestration for gradual API migration
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Background: Upcoming API version changes introduce subtle behavioral differences in streaming semantics and tool/function call handoff. We need a runtime-side proxy adapter plus an orchestrated set of behavior flags so customer traffic can be migrated incrementally without user-visible regressions. This ticket covers the engineering design and implementation of a lightweight streaming proxy adapter, the flag orchestration framework for phased opt-in, and the automated regression tests and telemetry that validate parity between old and new behavior. Goals: 1) Deploy an in-line proxy adapter that can translate legacy streaming frames to the new stream protocol and vice versa, 2) Provide a flag orchestration layer to route per-customer/per-route traffic to adapter vs native runtime, 3) Implement end-to-end CI and replay tests that exercise tool/function calling across both paths and detect semantic drift, 4) Produce runbook and rollback hooks for canary/gradual migration.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter translates legacy streaming chunk headers and tool-call boundaries with <= 1% message reorder or truncation errors in synthetic replay
Flag orchestration supports customer-level and route-level policies with rollout percentages and time windows
Integration test suite includes 200+ replayed conversations that validate structured output conformance and tool-call ordering across both paths
No P0 customer-facing incidents for test tenants after 2 weeks of canary at 10% traffic
Dashboard shows per-flag delta metrics for latency, token-cost, and semantic-regression alerts
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dry-run - run adapter with internal tenants using traffic shadowing only (no responses returned) for 3 days
Phase 1: Canary - enable adapter+flag for 1% of non-critical customers for 48 hours with tight SLO gates
Phase 2: Gradual ramp - increase to 10% for 7 days while monitoring regression signals and error budgets
Phase 3: Customer opt-in - enable per-customer opt-in control in Console and surface SDK helper methods
Phase 4: Full switch - toggle default behavior for new deployments and begin deprecation countdown for legacy path
test_plan: Create replay harness that replays historical streaming interactions including tool calls and structured outputs
Fuzz test stream boundaries and intentional mid-stream protocol interruptions to validate adapter robustness
Cross-path consistency tests: replay same session through legacy path and adapter path, diff structured outputs using schema-aware comparator
CI job: nightly regression matrix across models (small/medium/large), sequence lengths, and quantization profiles
Add synthetic customers to staging with automatic validators that assert tool-call idempotency and ordering
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Adapter introduces extra latency for streaming customers. Mitigation: implement fast-path bypass for small frames and measure p95/p99 separately.
Risk: Tool-call boundary semantics differ and cause downstream integration failures. Mitigation: add strict ordering checks, schema validators, and an automatic fallback to legacy path on mismatch.
Risk: Flags accidentally enabled broadly. Mitigation: require two-step console approval and partner with SRE to add circuit-breaker gates tied to error-budget metrics.
Risk: Incomplete test coverage for rare sequence patterns. Mitigation: use production sampling to seed the replay corpus and expand cases found in post-canary incidents.
